tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Step 1. Quote Monero (XMR) <-> native USDC on Arbitrum One; no account or API key. Creates no order. Quotes are estimates. Buy XMR ("get me 1 XMR"): {direction:"u2x", receiveAmount:"1"}. Sell XMR: {direction:"x2u", amount:"0.5"}. direction plus exactly one of amount (what the user sends) or receiveA

tools.name: create_swap
tools.description: Step 2. Creates the order from get_quote's next.arguments (quoteId, plus to if the quote had none): one order per quote; moves no funds. An order cannot be cancelled; unfunded, it expires. Retry with the same arguments: the default idempotencyKey returns the same order. Fund once, only while payable

tools.name: get_swap_status
tools.description: Step 3. waiting_for_funding -> deposit_detected -> swap_processing -> completed, or refunding / terminal_failure (outcome refunded, failed, expired). Long-poll with waitSec 25 and sinceState = the last state; repeat next until terminal. Call it before funding or showing a deposit again. payment: wha

tools.name: get_funding_options
tools.description: Offline. How to get what the user sends: native USDC (not USDC.e) plus a little ETH for gas on Arbitrum One (u2x, default), or XMR in their own wallet (x2u). Pass from {chain, asset} (and amount) for one ordered checklist: quote, fund, re-quote (requoteOf).

tools.name: list_swaps
tools.description: Find orders when the orderId is lost (new chat, crash, unknown create outcome): pass the idempotencyKey create_swap used (default q_<quoteId>), or a sessionId. Read-only; addresses redacted; states can lag. Next: get_swap_status (live state, payable).

tools.name: plan_swap
tools.description: Optional, offline. Checks a partial request (direction, amount or receiveAmount, to) and returns the next question for the user. Skip it when you have what get_quote needs.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description: Optional. Chains, limits (provider minimum, USD), quote window, idempotency, validation rules, polling and the flow.

tools.name: create_support_ticket
tools.description: Stuck or failed swap, or a question: Support answers (get_support_ticket). Follow up with ticketId + replyToken. Never seed phrases or keys.

tools.name: get_support_ticket
tools.description: Support's answer on your ticket: status, awaiting, thread. Answers take minutes to hours.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Optional, after a swap: a rating 1-5 and a comment. The published average counts one rating per completed Swapper order; a comment marked publishable is shown after operator review.

tools.name: request_agent_key
tools.description: Optional. Issues a key that identifies this agent; quotes made with it (get_quote agentKey) and their orders use the agent fee (swapper://trust). The operator sees the name and contact given.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_swaps, get_support_ticket · Private data: get_quote, get_swap_status, get_funding_options, request_agent_key · Public sink: submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_swaps, get_support_ticket · Private data: get_quote, get_swap_status, get_funding_options, request_agent_key · Public sink: submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_quote" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
